---
title: Entities
description: Write or read every cached copy of a record with one call.
---

A todo is often in many queries at the same time: its own detail, a list
per filter, each loaded page of an infinite list. When it changes, every
copy should change. An entity is a record's schema with a way to get its
ID, and one write to it reaches every cached copy. This page shows how to
define one, write and read through it, and what a write reaches.

The examples import `api.ts` and `todos.ts` from
[Getting started](/docs/getting-started).

## Define an entity

Define it once, beside its schema, with what identifies a record:

```ts entities.ts
import { Entity } from "@monarcode/effetch-query";

import { Todo } from "./api.js";

export const Todos = Entity.make(Todo, { id: (todo) => todo.id });
```

`Entity.make` takes the schema and an `Entity.MakeOptions`, whose `id`
gets a todo's ID. A `Schema.Class` works as the schema too.

## Write or read a record by ID

Four functions take the entity:

- `Entity.update(Todos, id, f)` writes `f` of the todo into every cached
  query that holds it.
- `Entity.set(Todos, todo)` writes a whole todo, such as a mutation's
  result, over every copy with its ID.
- `Entity.remove(Todos, id)` drops the todo from every cached query that
  holds it.
- `Entity.get(Todos, id)` reads the newest cached copy, as an `Option`.
  Where copies differ, the one from the query fetched or written last
  wins. [Show a placeholder](/docs/queries/placeholders) uses it to fill a
  detail screen from a list.

Writes are recorded like `Query.update`'s, so in a mutation's
`optimistic` they're undone if the run fails. This mutation drops a todo
everywhere at once:

```ts
import { Fetch } from "@monarcode/effetch";
import { Entity } from "@monarcode/effetch-query";

import { Todos } from "./entities.js";
import { api, todos } from "./todos.js";

export const deleteTodo = api.mutation(Fetch.endpoint("DELETE /todos/:id"), {
  optimistic: ({ params }) => Entity.remove(Todos, Number(params.id)),
  // The lists' totals come from the server.
  invalidates: [todos],
});
```

IDs are compared with `Equal.equals`, so convert a route param first, with
`Number(params.id)`: a number and a string don't match.

Neither `Entity.set` nor `Entity.remove` changes which records a list
holds or how many:

- `Entity.set` adds the todo to no list. Invalidate the lists it should
  join.
- `Entity.remove` leaves totals as they were, so invalidate the lists
  too, and count an infinite query's next page from its params, not its
  length.

<Accordions type="multiple">
  <Accordion title="Details: where Entity.remove can't drop a record">
    `Entity.remove` drops the todo from arrays and records. An optional field
    loses it: an `optionalKey` field loses its key, and a `NullOr` or `optional`
    field becomes `null` or `undefined`. Where the schema has no way to leave it
    out, it stays: a required field, a tuple's element, a non-empty array's last
    item, or a detail query's whole value.
  </Accordion>
</Accordions>

## What an entity write reaches

Nothing is normalized: each query keeps its own value, and an entity write
maps it. A write keeps each query's age, so it doesn't make a stale query
fresh or stop it from refetching. A query whose value doesn't change isn't
written. If `f` throws, nothing is written and the Effect dies with the
defect.

Some queries are left to their next fetch:

- a query that's invalidated and not in use, or that shows a failure;
- a query without a value;
- a query without a schema.

A query is found through its schema: an endpoint's `output`, or `schema`
on `Query.make`, `Query.family` and infinite queries. The entity is found
by its own schema, `Todo`, or `Todo` with annotations or checks added. A
schema built from `Todo`'s fields, such as
`Schema.Struct({ ...Todo.fields, extra })`, is a different schema, and
isn't the entity.

<Accordions type="multiple">
  <Accordion title="Details: where in a value an entity is found">
    The todo is found in arrays, tuples, records, struct fields, optional
    and `NullOr` fields, unions, nested and recursive schemas,
    `Schema.Class` instances and infinite queries' pages, on the decoded
    side of a schema that transforms.

    It isn't found inside `Option`, `Map` or other such types, after a
    tuple's rest element, or inside another copy of itself.

    A value sent from the server is reached after a query reads it: until
    then it's JSON, with no schema to search.

  </Accordion>
</Accordions>

## Responses in other shapes

Endpoints often return one record in different shapes: a search row with
its own field names, a detail wrapped in `data`. Decode each one to the
entity's schema with `Schema.decodeTo`. An entity is found on the decoded
side of a schema, so it's found in every query whose schema decodes to
it, whatever the wire shape:

```ts
import * as Schema from "effect/Schema";
import * as SchemaTransformation from "effect/SchemaTransformation";

import { Fetch } from "@monarcode/effetch";

import { Todo } from "./api.js";
import { api } from "./todos.js";

// What GET /search/todos sends for each todo. Only the fields that are
// read are declared: a response's other fields are ignored.
const SearchRow = Schema.Struct({
  todo_id: Schema.Finite,
  label: Schema.String,
  completed: Schema.Boolean,
});

// A search row as a Todo, so the Todos entity finds it.
export const TodoFromSearchRow = SearchRow.pipe(
  Schema.decodeTo(
    Todo,
    SchemaTransformation.transform({
      decode: (row) => ({
        id: row.todo_id,
        title: row.label,
        done: row.completed,
      }),
      // The mirror of decode, for server rendering.
      encode: (todo) => ({
        todo_id: todo.id,
        label: todo.title,
        completed: todo.done,
      }),
    }),
  ),
);

export const searchResults = api.query(
  Fetch.endpoint("GET /search/todos", {
    output: Schema.Array(TodoFromSearchRow),
  }),
);
```

`Entity.update(Todos, …)` writes the search results too, and `Entity.get`
reads them. Three things make it work:

- **Decode to the entity's own schema.** Import the one `Todo` the entity
  was made with. Another schema with the same fields isn't the entity.
- **Decode IDs to one type.** IDs are compared with `Equal.equals`, so a
  todo whose ID is `"1"` in one response and `1` in another is two todos.
- **Make `encode` the mirror of `decode` if you render on the server.** A
  query's value is sent to the browser in its wire shape, so its schema
  must encode the todo back, as
  [Schemas that transform](/docs/server-rendering/whats-sent#schemas-that-transform)
  explains. In an app that only runs in the browser, `encode` is never
  called.
